title: Rep. Nancy Mace urges tougher laws against tech-enabled exploitation
text:

Rep. Nancy Mace urges tougher laws against tech-enabled exploitation
Rep. Nancy Mace used social media on October 15 to call attention to gaps in federal law regarding tech-enabled exploitation crimes and suggested expanding investigations within Congress.
Rep. Nancy Mace, a U.S. Congresswoman representing South Carolina’s 1st district since 2021, addressed concerns about the evolving risks posed by technology in a series of posts on October 15, 2026.
In her first statement, Mace highlighted the challenges created by advancements in technology and their impact on exploitation. She wrote, "Technology has changed how predators operate. Hidden cameras, AI-generated deepfakes, and social media have made exploitation easier than ever. Our laws shouldn't be stuck in the past. This is why we reintroduced the Increased Accountability for Nonconsensual Pornography Act." (October 15, 2026).
Later that day, Mace addressed current federal penalties for video voyeurism and called for reform. She stated, "A hidden camera can destroy a life. The punishment should fit the crime. Right now, federal video voyeurism law applies only in limited federal jurisdictions, such as certain federal land and property, vessels, and aircraft. The maximum penalty is just one year." (October 15, 2026).
In another post from the same date referencing congressional investigations involving Rep. Ilhan Omar and Rep. Cory Mills, Mace remarked, "While we’re investigating Ilhan, may we suggest Cory Mills next? Just a thought."
Mace's advocacy reflects ongoing debates over digital privacy laws and punishments for offenses involving new technologies such as hidden cameras or manipulated images generated by artificial intelligence.
Currently serving in Congress after succeeding Joe Cunningham in 2021—having previously served in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020—Mace was born in Fort Bragg in 1977 and resides in Charleston.
She graduated from The Citadel with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1999.
